tier_rationale: TP-Link's own product page describes this as an unmanaged 5-port switch: 'Plug and play, no configuration needed,' with no mention of the Omada SDN or Tether cloud/app ecosystem TP-Link uses for its managed and smart-home products. TP-Link's FCC grantee code (TE7) files intentional-radiator grants for its Wi-Fi routers, access points, mesh systems, and smart-home devices, and no such grant exists for the TL-SG105, consistent with a wired-only switch that contains no radio.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes, because there was never anything to unplug from except Ethernet cables. This is a dumb switch in the original sense: it forwards frames between five ports and does nothing else. No web interface, no app, no cloud account, and no firmware to update.

repairability.notes: Sealed metal-case switch with no user-serviceable parts; TP-Link backs it with a lifetime warranty instead of repairability.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: unmanaged switch, plug-and-play with no configuration needed, 5x gigabit RJ45 ports, no mention of any app or cloud service, fanless external-power design.

FCC grantee index for TP-Link Technologies (code TE7): filings are intentional-radiator grants for Wi-Fi routers, access points, range extenders, and smart-home devices. No grant exists for the TL-SG105 unmanaged switch, consistent with a device that has no radio.

open_questions: TP-Link has no entry in data/vendors.json. No incident of shipped-device function removal was found in this search, but a dedicated audit was not performed; note that TP-Link's networking equipment has separately drawn US government security scrutiny over supply-chain concerns, which is a different question from the vendor-conduct ledger this project tracks.
notes: One of several fixed-configuration 'desktop switch' models TP-Link sells alongside its cloud-managed Omada line; this SKU has no relationship to that ecosystem at all.
